At Box, we've been testing Gemini 4 Argon on our Box AI Complex Work eval for the past week. It's a huge upgrade over Gemini 3.1 Pro, jumping by 14 percentage points across all our tests, and firmly at the frontier. In our evaluation, we give the Box Agent (using Gemini 4 Argon) a variety of complex enterprise tasks involving enterprise documents in a range of industries. These tasks approximate the kind of hard, time-consuming work that knowledge workers do every day with their enterprise content. Gemini 4 is a huge leap on effectively every dimension of this work. Gemini 4 is far more capable on math, logic, analytics, and deep knowledge of a variety of business domains. It also works far harder to complete tasks fully without stopping short of the desired result. This is incredibly important for complex enterprise workflows that depend on robust task execution. Here are some example wins that we saw to put the improvements in perspective: * Financial services (+18 points): a funding-gap analysis for a family-owned company, where the brief spelled out every step of the projected statements, down to the interest on the bank loan and the overdraft for each year. Gemini 4 Argon built them exactly as specified, every line broken out and carried through to the funding gap. Gemini 3.1 Pro folded the interest into a single figure. * Healthcare (+25 points): an intensive care management plan where both models spotted a dangerous potassium level and a drug interaction. Only Gemini 4 Argon went back and pulled the offending drugs from the final regimen, so its plan actually matched its own diagnosis. * Technology (+37 points): a product performance review deciding which of two regional markets should have its cloud infrastructure optimized first. Gemini 4 Argon pulled the right month's user, retention and per-user figures for both regions and correctly flagged North America. Gemini 3.1 Pro often pulled the wrong rows, at one point reporting retention above 100%, and pointed the effort at the wrong region. * Energy (+16 points): an energy consumption report across two facilities that had to flag any gaps in the meter data. Gemini 4 Argon consistently caught that the data center's smart meter log stops in November. Gemini 3.1 Pro often missed it, at times declaring the logs complete. * Consumer products (+33 points): a product launch evaluation deciding which production expansion to fund. Gemini 4 Argon saw that existing inventory could bridge an early capacity gap, which made the smaller expansion viable with an earlier launch and a faster break-even. Gemini 3.1 Pro defaulted to the larger expansion and the later timeline. Gemini 4 Argon will be available in the Box AI Studio shortly for anyone to build custom Box Agents with.

Congrats Gemini team. Never bet against Google, the company that brought us Transformers and has overwhelming data, engineering talent, and compute. Everyone has, rightfully, pivoted back to coding. Coding agents are the killer app of AI. We're firmly at an elysium for developers and builders. Incidentally, getting Muse Wonder and Gemini Argon back-to-back is a reminder why you as an individual, and your company, should stay model agnostic and gateway-maxxx / fx-maxxx.

BREAKING: Gemini 4 is OUT and it's SURPRISINGLY GOOD?? I admit I was ready to trash this model qhen I saw the benchmarks but six of us at @every spent the past week testing it across coding, writing, design, and knowledge work, and were pleasantly surprsied. It’s a breakthrough if your company lives in Google’s ecosystem, and a strong option for frontier hoppers as a secondary model for certain tasks. I Here’s our vibe check: My new favorite writing partner. DeepMind hired professional writers with red pens to stamp out AI slop, and it worked. I use it to untangle structure and sharpen metaphors; it also taught me something new tracing in a few of my favorite books. It's got a natural feel for structure and detailed explanations that Astra and Opus lack. Shaky at refactors, fast on greenfield apps. At low effort on a from-scratch build, Gemini 4 built @kieranklaassen a working webcam heart-rate monitor in 35 minutes—matching Claude Opus 5.5’s quality and beating OpenAI’s models on that test. Where it cuts corners is self-verification and existing codebases. In 17 of Kieran’s 38 benchmark runs, it opened and closed its code-review step just 30 milliseconds apart instead of inspecting its changes. And on my Senior Engineer benchmark—refactoring a vibe coded slop codebase—it worked for four hours and 47 minutes and scored just 21% (versus 81% to 85% for GPT-6 Astra, Fable 5.1, Sonnet 5.5, and Opus 5.5). Not great. A 2026 model trapped in a 2025 harness. Antigravity, Google’s desktop agent app, feels six months to a year behind Claude Code and Codex—lacking cloud environments, SSH, a built-in browser, and smart permission checks (leaving you clicking constant pop-ups or using unrestricted "Turbo" mode). Net Result: I keep ChatGPT and Claude open day to day, and switch to Gemini 4 when I need an editorial partner to structure a tough essay, sharpen a metaphor, or close-read a book. Reach for it for live writing collaboration, fast low-effort prototypes, or steerable UI and dashboard design—ideally via Cursor or the API to skip Antigravity. When a model is good enough to force you to use a bad harness, it tells you something. State of Play: Google hadn’t shipped a major flagship upgrade since Gemini 3 Pro last November. For teams whose companies live in Google’s ecosystem, the model you can use inside your approved work tools finally belongs with the frontier pack. DeepMind closed the model gap; now Google needs to bring the app around it into 2026. Read our full vibe check: https://t.co/ZRITq2iFyl
